message.content: {"distractor_1":"Initialize the MCP client first and connect it to your agent to auto-discover server-hosted tools.","explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1":"Starting the MCP client first fails here because the client needs an already running MCP server (the tool registry) to list and wrap tools; the server must be initialized with FastMCP before the client can discover tools.","thinking_process1":"This is a believable mistake because both client and server are involved in tool integration and one might assume the client can be started to trigger discovery. The phrasing mirrors the correct answer's action-oriented style and technical density (MCP client, agent, auto-discover). Technically, initializing an MCP client is a valid step in other situations (for example when the server already exists or when using a pre-provisioned registry), so the approach is realistic. However, it is wrong for this scenario where you must create the MCP server first with FastMCP(\"server-name\") so the registry and @mcp.tool definitions are available for the client to list and wrap."}
